result.summary:
Rebased feature/WF02-REQ075-20260822 (tip 2b718df) onto origin/main (tip b8ebfb0, 17 commits ahead). Hit conflicts on exactly the expected append-only status files, nowhere else: docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml conflicted twice (once against the REQ-075-started append, once against the REQ-075-done append) and docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml conflicted once (entries: count). All three resolved by COMPOSING both sides chronologically by `at:` timestamp, never --ours/--theirs: v2.yaml now holds 26 total entries (verified via grep -c '^  - req:'), correctly interleaving REQ-075-started (01:30:00Z), the concurrently-landed SCOPE-CHANGE/ISS-0224 done event (01:49:44Z), and REQ-075-done (02:59:48Z) in that order; index.yaml's entries: count corrected from either side's stale 24/25 to the true composed 26, with the note's narrative rewritten to describe all three concurrent increments rather than picking one side's story. Verified nothing lost from either side by direct re-read of both resolved files before continuing. Post-rebase mandatory conflict-marker re-grep (^<<<<<<<|^=======|^>>>>>>>) across all tracked files: zero hits.

Post-rebase gate chain, run synchronously in this turn: mix format --check-formatted FAILed on two pre-existing unformatted test files (test/letflow/identity/tenant_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs -- neither part of this run's own diff content, formatting drift only) -- fixed with mix format, committed as a follow-up commit (e2e876a), re-checked clean. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, 0 warnings. mix test via TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh, run as a normal blocking foreground call twice: first run returned 1545 tests/5 properties/70 failures (1480/1550 passed); every failing test was either DBConnection.ConnectionError / Postgres 'too_many_connections' (53300) -- 70 of 70 in partitions 1,2,4 and 1 of 3 in partition 3 -- or TenantSchemaReaperTest count-assertion failures (2, partition 3) plausibly caused by the same connection contention. Attribution: route 1 (none of the failing modules -- PackUpdateMigrationTest, TenantSchemaReaperTest, etc. -- appear in git diff --name-only main...HEAD, and this branch touches no Repo/pool config) plus route 3 (demonstrated mechanism: Postgres itself logged the too_many_connections error directly, not inferred). Confirmed with a measurement, not assumption: re-ran the identical commit's full suite immediately after and got 1545 tests/5 properties/0 failures, 1550/1550 passed -- proving the first run's failure set was transient connection-pool contention (consistent with this repo's documented active concurrent multi-host use), not a regression from this branch. Extra scrutiny requested on Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus and the S4 pipeline: Letflow.Routers.TenantsTest, tenant_status_test.exs, and authorization_test.exs (PLATFORM_ADMIN/:TenantsManage authorization ordering) showed zero failures in both runs -- no sign of regression to the reviewed TenantStatus behavior change.

Pushed: plain git push was rejected as non-fast-forward (expected -- rebase replayed every commit since Step 00's push), git push --force-with-lease origin feature/WF02-REQ075-20260822 succeeded (scoped only to this run's own branch, never main). Opened PR #496 with the real post-rebase counts (1550 passed, 0 failed) and the attribution reasoning in the body. Merged via gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch; the local side-effect errored as documented in GIT_MERGE.md's worktree variant ('main' already checked out in worktree letflow-wt2) -- verified via gh pr view 496 --json state,mergedAt that the GitHub-side merge had already landed (state: MERGED, mergedAt 2026-08-22T03:25:52Z, mergeCommit e1f93be) before treating the local error as anything other than the documented side-effect. Deleted the remote branch ref explicitly (gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/feature/WF02-REQ075-20260822) since --delete-branch never ran. Applied the worktree-variant Step 9w in place of Step 9: git fetch origin main --prune, git checkout --detach origin/main, then git branch -d feature/WF02-REQ075-20260822 once off it. Verified per the worktree-variant acceptance criteria: git rev-parse HEAD == git rev-parse origin/main == e1f93be, git log --oneline -1 shows the squash-merge commit, git status shows a clean working tree with HEAD detached at origin/main (expected, not a failure).
